verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never writes this as an equality between two sums, because the right-hand side is the definition: the label sum is `WaveFamily.sum = finsum over I of f.term`, and each term's amplitude is already a function of the common-cover point, `f.amplitude I (commonLift h l (f.gap l) w)`. The paper's left-hand side is recovered pointwise by `up_down` -- upLift (Delta_l) (commonLift h l Delta_l w) = physicalLift h l w, whose Plane component is Y_{i(l)} -- so the two sums are equal term by term and the display follows by `finsum_congr` (or `Finset.sum_congr rfl`) in one line; no cancellation or reindexing is involved. The index set matches in the same sense as in (6.17): `masked_finsum_eventually` shows that near w the finsum is the finite sum over the Finset of labels active at w, which is L(U) for U small, up to labels versus bands. One difference of generality, recorded rather than charged: in `WaveFamily`/`RegularFamily` the gap `f.gap L` is an arbitrary per-label natural number constrained only by `gap_le : f.gap L <= Delta` and `gap_native : f.gap L <= nativeIndex h L.1`, so in that generality the H of two summands need not be the same torus, whereas the paper's display has one H for all l in L(U); a single common i_0 does appear at the actual instantiation (`padded_normal_germ`: gap = nativeIndex h (cellBand ...) - CommonWindow.index h n, common chart at CommonWindow.index h n). The extra generality is harmless for what the Lean proves there (`physical_sum_jet_bound`), which needs only a uniform bound on the gaps.
